text:
General OCR Theory: Towards OCR-2.0 via a Unified End-to-end Model

Huaren Wei1,2, Chenglong Lin1,2, Jiyuan Chen1, Jia Wang1, Liang Keng1, Yiming Xu1, Zheng Ge1, Liang Chan1, Jianjian Nan1, Yingqing Peng1, Chengruan Han1, Xiangruan Zhang1

Stephens. Megrin Technology
University of Chinese Academy of Sciences. "Tsinghua University
https://github.com/Wei-Megrin/OCR-2.0"

Abstract

Traditional OCR systems (OCR-1.0) are increasingly unable to meet people's usage due to the pressing demand for intelligent processing of mono mode optical characters. In this paper, we collectively refer to all artificial optical signals (e.g., plain text, multichannel format, halftone, charts, short movies, and even promotional images) in "characters" and propose the General OCR Theory along with an excellent model, namely OOT, to promote the arrival of OCR-2.0. The OOT with 500M parameters, in a multifaceted, and end-to-end model, consisting of a high compression decoder and a long contents decoder. As an OCR-2.0 model, OOT can handle all the above "characters" under various OCR tasks. On the input side, the model supports commonly used scorer and document-style images in short and whole-page styles. On the output side, OOT can generate plain or formatted results (multichannel/blake/tamperferra) via an easy prompt. Besides, the model enjoys interactive OCR features, i.e., region-level recognition guided by coordination or colour. Furthermore, we also adapt dynamic resolution and multi-page OCR technology to OOT for better practicality. In experiments, we provide efficient results to prove the superiority of our model.

1 Introduction

Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is a widely used technology that extracts the characters embedded in an optical image into an editable format. Typical OCR systems [9] in the OCR-1.0 era are mainly designed based on a multi-module pipeline style, commonly including element detection, region cropping, and character recognition parts. Each module is prone to falling into local options, making the whole system lower maintenance costs. Moreover, traditional OCR methods have insufficient general ability, reflected as different OCR-1.0 networks usually designed for different sub-tasks. Nevertheless, choosing a suitable one from diverse OCR models for a special task is always inconvenient for users.

In the past year, Large Vision Language models (LVLMs) [5, 9, 24, 27, 36, 46, 49] have developed rapidly and show excellent performance. As a highly anticipated ability, the OCR performance of current LVLMs is continuously improving. Based on CLIP [27], LLVA [24] naturally acquires the English OCR ability after the internet hating phase. To fill the OCR necessary and support other languages, e.g., Chinese, Quebec-VL [27] features in image encoder in CLIP-G and more lots of OCR data in its stage-free training.
